a: Mean is average; median is middle value and resists outliers better.
Mode is the most frequent value.
Correlation measures linear association; it is not causation.
A sample is a subset used to estimate a population.
A normal distribution is the familiar bell-shaped curve.
A p-value is the probability of data as extreme if the null were true.
A CI is a range of plausible values for a parameter.
Bias is systematic error that shifts estimates away from truth.
More complex models can cut bias but raise variance.
Outliers are unusual points; investigate before deleting.
